description.narrative: (Yemen): .Yemen's Systems, Health and Resilience Project (SHARP) is based on trust-building, self-reliance, and increased resilience to support stabilization efforts, strengthen systems, and engage local institutions to create the conditions for sustainability. SHARP, USAID's three-year flagship health activity, will take an integrated approach to reducing maternal, newborn, and child morbidity and mortality by focusing on the Minimum Service Package (MSP), emphasizing integrated reproductive, maternal and neonatal and child health (RMNCH) services, coupled with appropriate wrap-around support services that address life-threatening challenges for communities (e.g. malnutrition, cholera, diarrhea) with strong community engagement to change health seeking behaviors and health systems strengthening activities to create local ownership to sustain system enhancements post-project. SHARP will continue to foster an enabling environment and strengthen the health system by improving policies, strategies, practices, and increasing local ownership. ..With FY21 funds, SHARP will continue implementing core project activities launched last year in target governorates. SHARP will promote community outreach and engagement with quality, evidence-based messages via direct community engagement with local leaders and health care workers as well as media to introduce and reinforce key messages via community health counseling and services. SHARP will continue working both in the community with the help of the community midwives (CMWs) and the community reproductive health volunteers (CRHVs) and in the healthcare facilities to increase the availability of the MSP in targeted districts through a robust referral system and will continue the piloting of a subsidized voucher program and community-pooled savings plan. SHARP will also continue providing high-quality in-service training, implementing Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI), and strengthening management systems. .
